findings.finding: Selecting Codex enables semantic_intent on both the detector and scheduler. Selecting ChatGPT disables it.

The semantic-intent candidate branch admits nonempty remote utterances subject to its short-partial guard. The other branch uses the local grammar score and related-prefix fallback. Confirmation and clause-continuation logic also branch on semantic_intent.
Only Codex sets job.steer_supported true. This affects whether a running job can accept speculative question growth without replacement.
Codex stream_question carries a live update receiver; the ChatGPT branch sends one rendered prompt through streaming HTTP.

Existing scheduler test latest_semantic_reply_is_visible_while_older_code_is_still_streaming explicitly expects the old answer to remain visible until the new answer has a buffer. The observed CUDA-to-database stale display is consistent with this visibility policy.

comparisonDesign.finalPromptDiagnostic: Same captured final recognized question and explicit selected context; fresh Codex thread history, alternating route order, two repetitions. Excludes live question detection/steering and overlay timing.
comparisonDesign.actualBackendPlayback: Must retain and report the existing route-specific detection and update lifecycle; backend selection changes multiple parts of the system.

scope: Read-only source analysis and recorded-trace interpretation. Code paths describe architectural differences; no ChatGPT performance or accuracy superiority has been measured. This does not replace the pending live comparison.
